summary: Steuben fire tower in northern Schoolcraft County; staffed from 1930 and replaced by airplane detection in 1967. No source says whether it still stands.

facts.design: Steel tower (per a 1922 conservation report quoted by the Forest Lookouts page)
facts.status_note: Retired from fire detection by 1967; no source says whether the tower or any footings still stand.

access.note: No source describes access to the site.

events.note: Steel tower erected, per a 1922 conservation report. Conflicts with the CCC account of a tower built by Camp Steuben enrollees in 1933-37.
Buildings to house the fire lookouts erected at Steuben and Tie Hill towers.
Eugene Scott and Ernest Edwards began duties as fire wardens on the Steuben tower.
Fire at Martha Lake found and put out by the new wardens.
Forest Service use of the tower began; it had been state property before.
Forest Service airplane flights began; the air detection system was to replace eight fire towers, Steuben among them.

evidence.supports: Site is in Schoolcraft County, on Hiawatha National Forest land
Steel tower erected in 1921, per the 1922 report
evidence.quote: 1921: A steel tower was erected. (Biennial Report - The Department of Conservation - 1922)

evidence.supports: April 1929 (Escanaba Daily Press): housing for lookouts built at Steuben and Tie Hill
evidence.quote: April 13, 1929: "Buildings for housing for the fire lookouts were erected at Steuben and Tie Hill towers." (The Escanaba Daily Press)

evidence.supports: Spring 1930: Scott and Edwards began duties as fire wardens on the Steuben tower (item headed May 2, 1930)
evidence.quote: May 2, 1930: "Eugene Scott and Ernest Edwards began their duties as fire wardens on the Steuben tower Saturday.

evidence.supports: The next day, a fire at Martha Lake was found and put out
evidence.quote: They discovered a fire at Martha Lake at 3:30 o'clock Sunday and extinguished it.

evidence.supports: 1958 obituary (May 6, 1958): Scott was retired towerman for the Forest Service
evidence.quote: May 6, 1958: "Eugene Harvey Scott ... retired towerman for the U.S. Forest Service

evidence.supports: Scott served as towerman at Steuben for 29 years
evidence.quote: He served as towerman at Steuben for 29 years.
Camp Steuben in Schoolcraft County opened only 17 days later on May 4, 1933.

evidence.supports: CCC enrollees (the men at Camp Steuben) built a fire lookout tower near the town of Steuben
evidence.quote: The men at Camp Steuben were also engaged in these activities. They constructed a fire lookout tower near the town of Steuben in northern Schoolcraft County.

evidence.supports: Tower located near the small community of Steuben
evidence.quote: The other is the Steuben tower, located near the small community of Steuben.

evidence.supports: Forest Service use from 1937; state property before
evidence.quote: Its use by the Forest Service dates back to 1937. It too was state property before being released to the Forest Service.

evidence.supports: Weather Bureau used the tower; use discontinued about five years before 1967
evidence.quote: The U.S. Weather Bureau also used Steuben tower for gathering weather information, This operation was discontinued five years ago.

evidence.supports: Column dated November 17, 1967: Forest Service began scheduled airplane flights 'last month' (October 1967)
evidence.quote: 50 Years Ago November 17, 1967 Fire towers are becoming obsolete on the Hiawatha National Forest. Last month the U.S. Forest Service began scheduled airplane flights to aid in the detection of forest fires.

evidence.supports: Air detection system replaces eight fire towers
evidence.quote: The air detection system replaces eight fire towers, two of which are near Manistique.

evidence.supports: Fire towers becoming obsolete on the Hiawatha National Forest
evidence.quote: Fire towers are becoming obsolete on the Hiawatha National Forest.

notes_for_editor: Build date conflicts: the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1921 steel tower (from a 1922 report); the Schoolcraft County Historical Society says Camp Steuben enrollees built a lookout tower near the town in 1933-37. Neither source says whether one replaced the other, so the story keeps both. Fate after 1967 is unknown: no source found describes removal, sale, or what remains. The SCHS page carries a photo captioned 'Fire lookout tower at Steuben. Photo Courtesy Vivian Haight', but no image URL was captured, so no photo entry. Brief coordinates (46.1867, -86.435) were not checked. Wikipedia's Steuben entry redirects to Inwood Township and was not used. The Scott and Edwards item is headed May 2, 1930, but reports a Saturday start and a Sunday fire, which do not fit that date together, so the story says spring 1930 rather than a month.
